nodes.text: [A1][/A1]NAME
asprintf, dprintf, fprintf, printf, snprintf, sprintf — print formatted output
[A2][/A2]SYNOPSIS
[CODE3]
[A4][/A4]DESCRIPTION

The [I5]fprintf[/I5]() function shall place output on the named output [I6]stream[/I6]. The [I7]printf[/I7]() function shall place
output on the standard output stream [I8]stdout[/I8]. The [I9]sprintf[/I9]() function shall place output followed by the null byte,
[CODE10], in consecutive bytes starting at *[I11]s[/I11]; it is the user's responsibility to ensure that enough space is
available.

[S12][[A13]CX[/A13]][/S12] [IMG14] The
[I15]asprintf[/I15]() function shall be equivalent to [I16]sprintf[/I16](), except that the output string shall be written to dynamically
allocated memory, allocated as if by a call to [A17][I18]malloc[/I18]()[/A17], of sufficient length to hold
the resulting string, including a terminating null byte. If the call to [I19]asprintf[/I19]() is successful, the address of this
dynamically allocated string shall be stored in the location referenced by [I20]ptr[/I20].

The [I21]dprintf[/I21]() function shall be equivalent to the [I22]fprintf[/I22]() function, except that [I23]dprintf[/I23]() shall write
output to the file associated with the file descriptor specified by the [I24]fildes[/I24] argument rather than place output on a
stream. [IMG25]

The [I26]snprintf[/I26]() function shall be equivalent to [I27]sprintf[/I27](), with the addition of the [I28]n[/I28] argument which limits
the number of bytes written to the buffer referred to by [I29]s[/I29]. If [I30]n[/I30] is zero, nothing shall be written and [I31]s[/I31] may
be a null pointer. Otherwise, output bytes beyond the [I32]n[/I32]-1st shall be discarded instead of being written to the array, and a
null byte is written at the end of the bytes actually written into the array.

If copying takes place between objects that overlap as a result of a call to [I33]sprintf[/I33]() or [I34]snprintf[/I34](), the results
are undefined.

Each of these functions converts, formats, and prints its arguments under control of the [I35]format[/I35]. The application shall
ensure that the format is a character string, beginning and ending in its initial shift state, if any. The format is composed of
zero or more directives: [I36]ordinary characters[/I36], which are simply copied to the output stream, and [I37]conversion
specifications[/I37], each of which shall result in the fetching of zero or more arguments. The results are undefined if there are
insufficient arguments for the format. If the format is exhausted while arguments remain, the excess arguments shall be evaluated
but are otherwise ignored.

[S38][[A39]CX[/A39]][/S38] [IMG40]
Conversions can be applied to the [I41]n[/I41]th argument after the [I42]format[/I42] in the argument list, rather than to the next unused
argument. In this case, the conversion specifier character [CODE43] (see below) is replaced by the sequence
[CODE44][I45]n[/I45][CODE46], where [I47]n[/I47] is a decimal integer in the range [1,{NL_ARGMAX}], giving the position of the
argument in the argument list. This feature provides for the definition of format strings that select arguments in an order
appropriate to specific languages (see the EXAMPLES section).

The [I48]format[/I48] can contain either numbered argument conversion specifications (that is, those introduced by
[CODE49][I50]n[/I50][CODE51] and optionally containing the [CODE52][I53]m[/I53][CODE54] forms of field width and precision), or
unnumbered argument conversion specifications (that is, those introduced by the [CODE55] character and optionally containing the
[CODE56] form of field width and precision), but not both. The only exception to this is that [CODE57] can be mixed with the
[CODE58][I59]n[/I59][CODE60] form. The results of mixing numbered and unnumbered argument specifications in a format string are
undefined. When numbered argument specifications are used, specifying the [I61]N[/I61]th argument requires that all the leading
arguments, from the first to the ([I62]N-1[/I62])th, are specified in the format string.

In format strings containing the [CODE63][I64]n[/I64][CODE65] form of conversion specification, numbered arguments in the
argument list can be referenced from the format string as many times as required. [IMG66]

In format strings containing the [CODE67] form of conversion specification, each conversion specification uses the first
unused argument in the argument list.

[S68][[A69]CX[/A69]][/S68] [IMG70] All
forms of the [I71]fprintf[/I71]() functions allow for the insertion of a language-dependent radix character in the output string. The
radix character is defined in the current locale (category [I72]LC_NUMERIC ).[/I72] In the POSIX locale, or in a locale where the radix
character is not defined, the radix character shall default to a <period> ([CODE73]). [IMG74]

Each conversion specification is introduced by the [CODE75] character [S76][[A77]CX[/A77]][/S76] [IMG78]  or by the
character sequence [CODE79][I80]n[/I80][CODE81], [IMG82]  after
which the following appear in sequence:
Zero or more [I83]flags[/I83] (in any order), which modify the meaning of the conversion specification.

An optional minimum [I84]field width[/I84]. If the converted value has fewer bytes than the field width, it shall be padded with
<space> characters by default on the left; it shall be padded on the right if the left-adjustment flag ([CODE85]),
described below, is given to the field width. The field width takes the form of an <asterisk> ([CODE86]), [S87][[A88]CX[/A88]][/S87] [IMG89]  or in
conversion specifications introduced by [CODE90][I91]n[/I91][CODE92] the [CODE93][I94]m[/I94][CODE95] string, [IMG96] described below, or a decimal integer.

An optional [I97]precision[/I97] that gives the minimum number of digits to appear for the [CODE98], [CODE99], [CODE100],
[CODE101], [CODE102], and [CODE103] conversion specifiers; the number of digits to appear after the radix character for the
[CODE104], [CODE105], [CODE106], [CODE107], [CODE108], and [CODE109] conversion specifiers; the maximum number of significant
digits for the [CODE110] and [CODE111] conversion specifiers; or the maximum number of bytes to be printed from a string in the
[CODE112] [S113][[A114]XSI[/A114]][/S113] [IMG115]  and [CODE116] [IMG117]  conversion specifiers. The
precision takes the form of a <period> ([CODE118]) followed either by an <asterisk> ([CODE119]), [S120][[A121]CX[/A121]][/S120] [IMG122]  or in
conversion specifications introduced by [CODE123][I124]n[/I124][CODE125] the [CODE126][I127]m[/I127][CODE128] string, [IMG129] described below, or an optional decimal digit string, where a null digit
string is treated as zero. If a precision appears with any other conversion specifier, the behavior is undefined.
An optional length modifier that specifies the size of the argument.
A [I130]conversion specifier[/I130] character that indicates the type of conversion to be applied.

A field width, or precision, or both, may be indicated by an <asterisk> ([CODE131]). In this case an argument of type
[B132]int[/B132] supplies the field width or precision. Applications shall ensure that arguments specifying field width, or precision, or
both appear in that order before the argument, if any, to be converted. A negative field width is taken as a [CODE133] flag
followed by a positive field width. A negative precision is taken as if the precision were omitted. [S134][[A135]CX[/A135]][/S134] [IMG136]  In format
strings containing conversion specifications introduced by [CODE137][I138]n[/I138][CODE139], in addition to being indicated by the
decimal digit string, a field width may be indicated by the sequence [CODE140][I141]m[/I141][CODE142] and precision by the sequence
[CODE143][I144]m[/I144][CODE145], where [I146]m[/I146] is a decimal integer in the range [1,{NL_ARGMAX}] giving the position in the
argument list (after the [I147]format[/I147] argument) of an integer argument containing the field width or precision, for example:
The flag characters and their meanings are:
[CODE148]

[S149][[A150]CX[/A150]][/S149] [IMG151]
(The <apostrophe>.) The integer portion of the result of a decimal conversion ([CODE152], [CODE153], [CODE154],
[CODE155], [CODE156], [CODE157], or [CODE158]) shall be formatted with thousands' grouping characters. For other
conversions the behavior is undefined. The non-monetary grouping character is used. [IMG159]
[CODE160]

The result of the conversion shall be left-justified within the field. The conversion is right-justified if this flag is not
specified.
[CODE161]

The result of a signed conversion shall always begin with a sign ([CODE162] or [CODE163]). The conversion shall begin
with a sign only when a negative value is converted if this flag is not specified.
<space>
[CODE165]

Specifies that the value is to be converted to an alternative form. For [CODE166] conversion, it shall increase the precision,
if and only if necessary, to force the first digit of the result to be a zero (if the value and precision are both 0, a single 0 is
printed). For [CODE167] or [CODE168] conversion specifiers, a non-zero result shall have 0x (or 0X) prefixed to it. For
[CODE169], [CODE170], [CODE171], [CODE172], [CODE173], [CODE174], [CODE175], and [CODE176] conversion specifiers, the
result shall always contain a radix character, even if no digits follow the radix character. Without this flag, a radix character
appears in the result of these conversions only if a digit follows it. For [CODE177] and [CODE178] conversion specifiers,
trailing zeros shall [I179]not[/I179] be removed from the result as they normally are. For other conversion specifiers, the behavior is
undefined.
[CODE180]

For [CODE181], [CODE182], [CODE183], [CODE184], [CODE185], [CODE186], [CODE187], [CODE188], [CODE189], [CODE190],
[CODE191], [CODE192], [CODE193], and [CODE194] conversion specifiers, leading zeros (following any indication of sign or base)
are used to pad to the field width rather than performing space padding, except when converting an infinity or NaN. If the
[CODE195] and [CODE196] flags both appear, the [CODE197] flag is ignored. For [CODE198], [CODE199], [CODE200],
[CODE201], [CODE202], and [CODE203] conversion specifiers, if a precision is specified, the [CODE204] flag shall be ignored.
[S205][[A206]CX[/A206]][/S205] [IMG207]
 If the [CODE208] and <apostrophe> flags both appear, the grouping characters are inserted before zero padding. For
other conversions, the behavior is undefined. [IMG209]
The length modifiers and their meanings are:
[CODE210]

Specifies that a following [CODE211], [CODE212], [CODE213], [CODE214], [CODE215], or [CODE216] conversion specifier
applies to a [B217]signed char[/B217] or [B218]unsigned char[/B218] argument (the argument will have been promoted according to the integer
promotions, but its value shall be converted to [B219]signed char[/B219] or [B220]unsigned char[/B220] before printing); or that a following
[CODE221] conversion specifier applies to a pointer to a [B222]signed char[/B222] argument.
[CODE223]

Specifies that a following [CODE224], [CODE225], [CODE226], [CODE227], [CODE228], or [CODE229] conversion specifier
applies to a [B230]short[/B230] or [B231]unsigned short[/B231] argument (the argument will have been promoted according to the integer
promotions, but its value shall be converted to [B232]short[/B232] or [B233]unsigned short[/B233] before printing); or that a following
[CODE234] conversion specifier applies to a pointer to a [B235]short[/B235] argument.
[CODE236] (ell)

Specifies that a following [CODE237], [CODE238], [CODE239], [CODE240], [CODE241], or [CODE242] conversion specifier
applies to a [B243]long[/B243] or [B244]unsigned long[/B244] argument; that a following [CODE245] conversion specifier applies to a pointer to
a [B246]long[/B246] argument; that a following [CODE247] conversion specifier applies to a [B248]wint_t[/B248] argument; that a following
[CODE249] conversion specifier applies to a pointer to a [B250]wchar_t[/B250] argument; or has no effect on a following [CODE251],
[CODE252], [CODE253], [CODE254], [CODE255], [CODE256], [CODE257], or [CODE258] conversion specifier.
[CODE259] (ell-ell)

Specifies that a following [CODE260], [CODE261], [CODE262], [CODE263], [CODE264], or [CODE265] conversion specifier applies
to a [B266]long long[/B266] or [B267]unsigned long long[/B267] argument; or that a following [CODE268] conversion specifier applies to a
pointer to a [B269]long long[/B269] argument.
[CODE270]

Specifies that a following [CODE271], [CODE272], [CODE273], [CODE274], [CODE275], or [CODE276] conversion specifier
applies to an [B277]intmax_t[/B277] or [B278]uintmax_t[/B278] argument; or that a following [CODE279] conversion specifier applies to a
pointer to an [B280]intmax_t[/B280] argument.
[CODE281]

Specifies that a following [CODE282], [CODE283], [CODE284], [CODE285], [CODE286], or [CODE287] conversion specifier
applies to a [B288]size_t[/B288] or the corresponding signed integer type argument; or that a following [CODE289] conversion specifier
applies to a pointer to a signed integer type corresponding to a [B290]size_t[/B290] argument.
[CODE291]

Specifies that a following [CODE292], [CODE293], [CODE294], [CODE295], [CODE296], or [CODE297] conversion specifier
applies to a [B298]ptrdiff_t[/B298] or the corresponding [B299]unsigned[/B299] type argument; or that a following [CODE300] conversion
specifier applies to a pointer to a [B301]ptrdiff_t[/B301] argument.
[CODE302]

Specifies that a following [CODE303], [CODE304], [CODE305], [CODE306], [CODE307], [CODE308], [CODE309], or [CODE310]
conversion specifier applies to a [B311]long double[/B311] argument.
If a length modifier appears with any conversion specifier other than as specified above, the behavior is undefined.
The conversion specifiers and their meanings are:
[CODE312], [CODE313]

The [B314]int[/B314] argument shall be converted to a signed decimal in the style [CODE315][I316]dddd[/I316][CODE317]. The precision
specifies the minimum number of digits to appear; if the value being converted can be represented in fewer digits, it shall be
expanded with leading zeros. The default precision is 1. The result of converting zero with an explicit precision of zero shall be
no characters.
[CODE318]

The [B319]unsigned[/B319] argument shall be converted to unsigned octal format in the style [CODE320][I321]dddd[/I321][CODE322]. The
precision specifies the minimum number of digits to appear; if the value being converted can be represented in fewer digits, it
shall be expanded with leading zeros. The default precision is 1. The result of converting zero with an explicit precision of zero
shall be no characters.
[CODE323]

The [B324]unsigned[/B324] argument shall be converted to unsigned decimal format in the style [CODE325][I326]dddd[/I326][CODE327]. The
precision specifies the minimum number of digits to appear; if the value being converted can be represented in fewer digits, it
shall be expanded with leading zeros. The default precision is 1. The result of converting zero with an explicit precision of zero
shall be no characters.
[CODE328]

The [B329]unsigned[/B329] argument shall be converted to unsigned hexadecimal format in the style [CODE330][I331]dddd[/I331][CODE332];
the letters [CODE333] are used. The precision specifies the minimum number of digits to appear; if the value being
converted can be represented in fewer digits, it shall be expanded with leading zeros. The default precision is 1. The result of
converting zero with an explicit precision of zero shall be no characters.
[CODE334]

Equivalent to the [CODE335] conversion specifier, except that letters [CODE336] are used instead of
[CODE337].
[CODE338], [CODE339]

A [B340]double[/B340] argument representing an infinity shall be converted in one of the styles [CODE341] or
[CODE342]; which style is implementation-defined. A [B343]double[/B343] argument representing a NaN shall be converted in
one of the styles [CODE344][I345]n-char-sequence[/I345][CODE346] or [CODE347]; which style, and the meaning of any
[I348]n-char-sequence[/I348], is implementation-defined. The [CODE349] conversion specifier produces [CODE350],
[CODE351], or [CODE352] instead of [CODE353], [CODE354], or [CODE355], respectively.
[CODE356], [CODE357]

A [B358]double[/B358] argument representing an infinity or NaN shall be converted in the style of an [CODE359] or [CODE360]
conversion specifier.
[CODE361], [CODE362]

If [CODE363]>[I364]X[/I364]>=-4, the conversion shall be with style [CODE365] (or [CODE366]) and precision
[CODE367]-([I368]X[/I368]+1).
Otherwise, the conversion shall be with style [CODE369] (or [CODE370]) and precision [CODE371]-1.

Finally, unless the [CODE372] flag is used, any trailing zeros shall be removed from the fractional portion of the result and
the decimal-point character shall be removed if there is no fractional portion remaining.

A [B373]double[/B373] argument representing an infinity or NaN shall be converted in the style of an [CODE374] or [CODE375]
conversion specifier.
[CODE376], [CODE377]

A [B378]double[/B378] argument representing an infinity or NaN shall be converted in the style of an [CODE379] or [CODE380]
conversion specifier.
[CODE381]

If an [CODE382] (ell) qualifier is present, [S383][[A384]CX[/A384]][/S383] [IMG385]  the [B386]wint_t[/B386] argument shall be converted to a multi-byte
sequence as if by a call to [A387][I388]wcrtomb[/I388]()[/A387] with a pointer to storage of at least
MB_CUR_MAX bytes, the [B389]wint_t[/B389] argument converted to [B390]wchar_t[/B390], and an initial shift state, and the resulting byte(s)
written. [IMG391]
[CODE392]

If an [CODE393] (ell) qualifier is present, the argument shall be a pointer to an array of type [B394]wchar_t[/B394]. Wide characters
from the array shall be converted to characters (each as if by a call to the [A395][I396]wcrtomb[/I396]()[/A395] function, with the conversion state described by an [B397]mbstate_t[/B397] object
initialized to zero before the first wide character is converted) up to and including a terminating null wide character. The
resulting characters shall be written up to (but not including) the terminating null character (byte). If no precision is
specified, the application shall ensure that the array contains a null wide character. If a precision is specified, no more than
that many characters (bytes) shall be written (including shift sequences, if any), and the array shall contain a null wide
character if, to equal the character sequence length given by the precision, the function would need to access a wide character one
past the end of the array. In no case shall a partial character be written.
[CODE398]

The argument shall be a pointer to [B399]void[/B399]. The value of the pointer is converted to a sequence of printable characters, in
an implementation-defined manner.
[CODE400]

The argument shall be a pointer to an integer into which is written the number of bytes written to the output so far by this
call to one of the [I401]fprintf[/I401]() functions. No argument is converted.
[CODE402]

[S403][[A404]XSI[/A404]][/S403] [IMG405]
Equivalent to [CODE406]. [IMG407]
[CODE408]

[S409][[A410]XSI[/A410]][/S409] [IMG411]
Equivalent to [CODE412]. [IMG413]
[CODE414]

Write a [CODE415] character; no argument shall be converted. The application shall ensure that the complete conversion
specification is [CODE416].

If a conversion specification does not match one of the above forms, the behavior is undefined. If any argument is not the
correct type for the corresponding conversion specification, the behavior is undefined.

In no case shall a nonexistent or small field width cause truncation of a field; if the result of a conversion is wider than the
field width, the field shall be expanded to contain the conversion result. Characters generated by [I417]fprintf[/I417]() and
[I418]printf[/I418]() are printed as if [A419][I420]fputc[/I420]()[/A419] had been called.

For the [CODE421] and [CODE422] conversion specifiers, if FLT_RADIX is a power of 2, the value shall be correctly rounded to a
hexadecimal floating number with the given precision.

For [CODE423] and [CODE424] conversions, if FLT_RADIX is not a power of 2 and the result is not exactly representable in the
given precision, the result should be one of the two adjacent numbers in hexadecimal floating style with the given precision, with
the extra stipulation that the error should have a correct sign for the current rounding direction.

For the [CODE425], [CODE426], [CODE427], [CODE428], [CODE429], and [CODE430] conversion specifiers, if the number of
significant decimal digits is at most DECIMAL_DIG, then the result should be correctly rounded. If the number of significant
decimal digits is more than DECIMAL_DIG but the source value is exactly representable with DECIMAL_DIG digits, then the result
should be an exact representation with trailing zeros. Otherwise, the source value is bounded by two adjacent decimal strings
[I431]L[/I431] < [I432]U[/I432], both having DECIMAL_DIG significant digits; the value of the resultant decimal string [I433]D[/I433] should
satisfy [I434]L[/I434] <= [I435]D[/I435] <= [I436]U[/I436], with the extra stipulation that the error should have a correct sign for the
current rounding direction.

[S437][[A438]CX[/A438]][/S437] [IMG439] The
last data modification and last file status change timestamps of the file shall be marked for update:

Between the call to a successful execution of [I440]fprintf[/I440]() or [I441]printf[/I441]() and the next successful completion of a call
to [A442][I443]fflush[/I443]()[/A442] or [A444][I445]fclose[/I445]()[/A444] on the same
stream or a call to [A446][I447]exit[/I447]()[/A446] or [A448][I449]abort[/I449]()[/A448]
Upon successful completion of a call to [I450]dprintf[/I450]()
[A451][/A451]RETURN VALUE

Upon successful completion, the [S452][[A453]CX[/A453]][/S452] [IMG454] [I455]dprintf[/I455](), [IMG456] [I457]fprintf[/I457](),
and [I458]printf[/I458]() functions shall return the number of bytes transmitted.

[S459][[A460]CX[/A460]][/S459] [IMG461]
Upon successful completion, the [I462]asprintf[/I462]() function shall return the number of bytes written to the allocated string stored
in the location referenced by [I463]ptr[/I463], excluding the terminating null byte. [IMG464]

Upon successful completion, the [I465]sprintf[/I465]() function shall return the number of bytes written to [I466]s[/I466], excluding the
terminating null byte.

Upon successful completion, the [I467]snprintf[/I467]() function shall return the number of bytes that would be written to [I468]s[/I468]
had [I469]n[/I469] been sufficiently large excluding the terminating null byte.

If an error was encountered, these functions shall return a negative value [S470][[A471]CX[/A471]][/S470] [IMG472]  and set
[I473]errno[/I473] to indicate the error. For [I474]asprintf[/I474](), if memory allocation was not possible, or if some other error occurs,
the function shall return a negative value, and the contents of the location referenced by [I475]ptr[/I475] are undefined, but shall not
refer to allocated memory. [IMG476]

If the value of [I477]n[/I477] is zero on a call to [I478]snprintf[/I478](), nothing shall be written, the number of bytes that would have
been written had [I479]n[/I479] been sufficiently large excluding the terminating null shall be returned, and [I480]s[/I480] may be a null
pointer.

The next call to [I529]printf[/I529]() outputs the owner's name if it is found using [A530][I531]getpwuid[/I531]()[/A530]; the [A532][I533]getpwuid[/I533]()[/A532] function shall

[A542][/A542]Printing a Localized Date String

The following example gets a localized date string. The [A543][I544]nl_langinfo[/I544]()[/A543]
function shall return the localized date string, which specifies the order and layout of the date. The [A545][I546]strftime[/I546]()[/A545] function takes this information and, using the [B547]tm[/B547] structure for values,
places the date and time information into [I548]datestring[/I548]. The [I549]printf[/I549]() function then outputs [I550]datestring[/I550] and the
name of the entry.
[A551][/A551]Printing Error Information
The following example uses [I552]fprintf[/I552]() to write error information to standard error.

In the first group of calls, the program tries to open the password lock file named [B553]LOCKFILE[/B553]. If the file already exists,
this is an error, as indicated by the O_EXCL flag on the [A554][I555]open[/I555]()[/A554] function. If the call
fails, the program assumes that someone else is updating the password file, and the program exits.

The next group of calls saves a new password file as the current password file by creating a link between [B556]LOCKFILE[/B556] and
the new password file [B557]PASSWDFILE[/B557].

[A578][/A578]APPLICATION USAGE

If the application calling [I579]fprintf[/I579]() has any objects of type [B580]wint_t[/B580] or [B581]wchar_t[/B581], it must also include the
[A582][I583]<wchar.h>[/I583][/A582] header to have these objects defined.
The space allocated by a successful call to [I584]asprintf[/I584]() should be subsequently freed by a call to [A585][I586]free[/I586]()[/A585].
[A587][/A587]RATIONALE

If an implementation detects that there are insufficient arguments for the format, it is recommended that the function should
fail and report an [EINVAL] error.

The behavior specified for the [CODE588] conversion differs slightly from the specification in the ISO C standard, in
that printing the null wide character produces a null byte instead of 0 bytes of output as would be required by a strict reading of
the ISO C standard's direction to behave as if applying the [CODE589] specifier to a [B590]wchar_t[/B590] array whose first
element is the null wide character. Requiring a multi-byte output for every possible wide character, including the null character,
matches historical practice, and provides consistency with [CODE591] in [I592]fprintf[/I592]() and with both [CODE593] and
[CODE594] in [A595][I596]fwprintf[/I596]()[/A595]. It is anticipated that a future edition of the
ISO C standard will change to match the behavior specified here.
